_doc: State temporary disability (TDI/SDI) and paid family and medical leave (PFML) programs, read on the agency pages and statutes on 2026-10-20 (quotes in notes/releve-conges-*.md). aww: how the engine turns the reader's pay into the program's average weekly wage (base hq = highest quarter, sum2 = two highest quarters, bpw = pay over the base year; div = divisor); exact = the agency's own definition, otherwise awwNote says what is simplified. tiers: [[up to this weekly wage, replacement rate], ...], the last with null. floor: a flat amount the benefit cannot fall under above the first tier (California). weeks: maximum weeks by reason; waiting: unpaid days before benefits by reason, only where read on an official page. contrib: employee share of the 2026 premium (rate on wages up to cap; cap null = no ceiling; weeklyMax = cap per week). status coming = no benefit paid on 2026-10-20. mode band (California): the whole weekly wage is replaced at the rate of its band, not tier by tier.

programs.name: California State Disability Insurance (DI)
programs.rule: 90% of high-quarter wages ÷ 13 when the high quarter is $16,279.90 or less; above that, the greater of 70% of high-quarter wages ÷ 13 or $1,127; between $50 and $1,765 a week

programs.name: California Paid Family Leave (PFL)
programs.rule: same table as SDI: 90% or 70% of high-quarter wages ÷ 13, between $50 and $1,765 a week, up to 8 weeks in 12 months

programs.name: New York Disability Benefits Law (DBL)
programs.awwNote: New York averages the last eight weeks worked; the engine uses your regular weekly pay.
programs.rule: 50% of the average weekly wage of the last eight weeks, no more than $170 a week, for up to 26 weeks

programs.name: New York Paid Family Leave
programs.awwNote: New York averages the last eight weeks worked; the engine uses your regular weekly pay.
programs.rule: 67% of the average weekly wage, up to 67% of the 2026 state average weekly wage of $1,833.63, so at most $1,228.53 a week

programs.name: New Jersey Temporary Disability Insurance
programs.awwNote: New Jersey averages the weeks worked in the base year; the engine assumes a full year of work.
programs.rule: 85% of the average weekly wage, up to $1,119 a week in 2026, for up to 26 weeks

programs.name: New Jersey Family Leave Insurance
programs.awwNote: New Jersey averages the weeks worked in the base year; the engine assumes a full year of work.
programs.rule: 85% of the average weekly wage, up to $1,119 a week in 2026, for 12 consecutive weeks or 8 weeks taken intermittently

programs.name: Rhode Island Temporary Disability Insurance
programs.minNote: $148 is the minimum read for claims from January 2026; the July 2026 minimum was not found.
programs.rule: 4.62% of the wages of the highest quarter of the base period, up to $1,150 a week for claims from July 1, 2026 ($1,552 with five dependents)

programs.name: Rhode Island Temporary Caregiver Insurance
programs.minNote: $148 is the minimum read for claims from January 2026; the July 2026 minimum was not found.
programs.rule: same rate as TDI, up to 8 weeks, counted within the 30 weeks of the benefit year

programs.name: Hawaii Temporary Disability Insurance
programs.awwNote: Hawaii averages the weeks of employment before the disability; the engine uses your regular weekly pay.
programs.rule: 58% of the average weekly wage, up to $871 a week in 2026, from the eighth day, for up to 26 weeks

programs.name: Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine averages your two highest quarters, the method Washington uses for most workers.
programs.rule: 90% of the weekly wage up to half the state average weekly wage, plus 50% of the part above, up to $1,647 a week in 2026

programs.name: Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine averages your two highest quarters, the individual average weekly wage Massachusetts describes.

contrib.note: the most an employer may deduct; wage cap not modeled

programs.rule: 80% of the weekly wage up to half the 2026 state average weekly wage of $1,922.48, plus 50% above, up to $1,230.39 a week

programs.name: Connecticut Paid Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine averages your two highest quarters.
programs.rule: 95% of the weekly wage up to 40 times the Connecticut minimum wage ($677.60), plus 60% above, capped at 60 times the minimum wage ($1,016.40)

programs.name: Paid Leave Oregon
programs.awwNote: The engine divides your base-year pay by 52.
programs.rule: 100% of the weekly wage up to 65% of the state average weekly wage ($1,410.13), plus 50% above, between $70.51 and $1,692.16 a week for benefit years from June 28, 2026

programs.name: Colorado Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)
programs.awwNote: The engine averages your two highest quarters.
programs.rule: 90% of the weekly wage up to $804.46, plus 50% above, up to $1,448.02 a week from July 1, 2026

programs.name: Minnesota Paid Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine divides your highest quarter by 13.
programs.rule: 90% of the first $711.50 of weekly wage, 66% of the next $711.50 and 55% above, up to $1,423 a week, since January 1, 2026

programs.name: Delaware Paid Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine divides your yearly pay by 52.

contrib.note: at most half of the 0.8% premium

programs.rule: 80% of the average weekly wage, up to $900 a week in 2026 and 2027, since January 1, 2026

programs.name: Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine averages your two highest quarters.
programs.maxNote: The law caps the benefit at the state average weekly wage, $1,249.12 from July 1, 2026; Maine's own chart rounds it to $1,250, and the cap at the May 2026 launch was $1,199.

contrib.note: at most half of the 1% premium

programs.rule: 90% of the weekly wage up to half the state average weekly wage, plus 66% above, capped at the state average weekly wage, for leave from May 1, 2026

programs.name: DC Paid Family Leave
programs.awwNote: The engine divides your yearly pay by 52.
programs.rule: 90% of the weekly wage up to 150% of 40 hours at the DC minimum wage ($1,104), plus 50% above, capped at $1,100 a week from October 1, 2026

programs.name: Maryland Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)
programs.rule: to come: contributions from January 1, 2027, benefits from January 1, 2028; weekly amounts not yet published
